prompt.context: Our client is the Chicago Transit Authority (CTA). They have received $300MM and want us to identify which of the 20 different technology projects should be implemented and in which order. Currently, they have a 30-year-old Mainframe system. They have written bridge/translation code to interface with some of their newer systems. However, everything is controlled by this mainframe.
prompt.question: How would you advise the CTA on which of the 20 technology projects to implement and in which order?

clarifying_info.q: Is CTA focused primarily on cost savings or service quality?
clarifying_info.a: CTA is a public service. They may take on negative NPV projects if it serves the public. They may also prioritize based on public, not financial, needs.

clarifying_info.q: Will CTA reduce headcount as part of this technology transformation?
clarifying_info.a: CTA does not want to fire its employees.

clarifying_info.q: What is the skill level of CTA's technology staff?
clarifying_info.a: Almost all CTA technology employees know only old mainframe systems.

clarifying_info.q: Is the original mainframe code documented?
clarifying_info.a: No one knows the original code for the mainframe system. Bug fixes are being done by people who only know bits and pieces of the system.

clarifying_info.q: Does CTA have enough budget to fund all 20 projects?
clarifying_info.a: CTA has enough money to do all 20 projects.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any particularly high-profile projects among the 20?
clarifying_info.a: There are two high-profile projects: an ERP system and a Smartcard for toll booths.

clarifying_info.q: How old is the mainframe and is support available?
clarifying_info.a: The mainframe system in use is from the 1970s and there are not many people who can support it. However, almost all systems are controlled by this system.

framework: Assess the impact of each project on CTA's technology infrastructure across three dimensions: (1) impact on the core mainframe system, (2) impact on translation/bridge software, (3) impact/requirements for new systems
Estimate person-hours required to implement each project

Prioritize projects using four criteria: (1) criticality to public needs, (2) impact on critical existing infrastructure, (3) economic impact measured in dollars and person-hours, (4) personnel training required for new systems
Apply the prioritization criteria to the two high-profile projects (ERP and Smartcard) as a worked example

questions.prompt: How would you structure your approach to evaluating which of the 20 projects to prioritize?
questions.guidance: A strong answer recognizes that CTA is a public-service entity, so public benefit and legal obligations take precedence over pure financial return. The candidate should propose a two-step framework: first map each project's interaction with the legacy mainframe infrastructure, then rank projects using a multi-criteria scoring model that includes public impact, infrastructure risk, cost/effort, and training burden. The candidate should also flag that some projects may be legally mandated regardless of NPV.

questions.prompt: Of the two high-profile projects—ERP system and Smartcard for toll booths—which would you prioritize and why?
questions.guidance: A strong answer applies the four prioritization criteria explicitly. The Smartcard project is more critical because it directly serves the public (fare collection, rider convenience) and may also have infrastructure or legal implications. ERP is an internal operations improvement and, while valuable, is less visible to riders and less tied to public-service obligations. The candidate should reason through each criterion rather than defaulting to a generic answer.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks and complications should CTA anticipate when executing this technology transformation?

categories.name: Legacy system risk
ideas: No one fully understands the original mainframe code, so changes may cause unexpected failures
Bug fixes done piecemeal increase the risk of cascading errors
Dependency mapping between mainframe and bridge/translation code may be incomplete

categories.name: Workforce and change management
ideas: Staff know only old mainframe systems; retraining takes time and budget
CTA's no-layoff policy means staff must be retrained rather than replaced
Resistance to change from long-tenured employees familiar with legacy processes

categories.name: Project execution
ideas: Sequencing matters: projects that touch the mainframe core must be coordinated carefully
Parallel implementation of multiple projects may overwhelm limited IT capacity
Scope creep on high-profile projects like ERP can derail timelines

categories.name: Public service continuity
ideas: Any system outage directly impacts riders and public perception
Mission-critical systems (fare collection, scheduling) cannot tolerate extended downtime
Some projects may be legally required regardless of readiness

categories.name: Financial / governance
ideas: $300MM is fixed; cost overruns on early projects could crowd out later ones
Public accountability requires transparent prioritization rationale
Stakeholder alignment across city government, unions, and riders is needed

recommendation: Prioritize projects by public impact and infrastructure criticality first, not by financial return, given CTA's public-service mandate
Implement the Smartcard project before the ERP system because it directly benefits riders and is more closely tied to core public operations
Phase the 20 projects into waves based on mainframe dependency and staff training requirements, beginning with projects that reduce reliance on the most fragile parts of the legacy system
risks: Mainframe instability during transition could disrupt transit operations
Staff retraining bottleneck may slow implementation of all 20 projects
Legally mandated projects with negative NPV will consume budget regardless of strategic priority
next_steps: Conduct a full dependency audit of the mainframe and all bridge/translation code
Develop a skills inventory and retraining plan for all CTA technology staff
Create a phased project roadmap with explicit sequencing logic tied to the four prioritization criteria
